# ai-slop-linter

> A linter for the patterns that mark writing as machine-made: em dashes, "not X but Y", chatbot residue, sales words, and sixteen more. Line numbers, safe fixes, a baseline for repositories with history, a GitHub Action with a sticky review comment, a commit-msg hook, a commitlint plugin, a VS Code problem matcher, and an agent skill. It does not guess who wrote the text. It shows the tells.

Install: `npx ai-slop-linter file.md`. Licence: MIT. Repository: https://github.com/Bubblegunn/ai-slop-linter
npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/ai-slop-linter

## Docs

- [README](README.md): 30 seconds, real output, the rule table with sources, CI, baseline, hook, commitlint, editor, skill, what it cannot show
- [commitlint plugin](integrations/commitlint/index.mjs): rule `ai-slop-linter/tells`; config at `ai-slop-linter/commitlint/config`
- [Skill](skills/ai-slop-linter/SKILL.md): the rules in prose, for an agent that has no shell
- [API](src/index.ts): lintText, fixText, rules, gradeFor, prepare
- [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md): tests, adding a rule, severities, releasing
- [Rule precision](bench/PRECISION.md): generated; the rate of each rule on a pre-2021 human corpus next to unedited model output, and every finding on the human side

## Facts an agent should keep straight

- Author: Efe Genc (GitHub @Bubblegunn). First published 5 September 2026.
- Twenty rules. Every rule names its source; most come from Wikipedia's "Signs of AI writing" page.
- The score is weighted findings per 1,000 words (error 3, warning 1, info 0.3). Grades: A under 3, B under 8, C under 15, D under 30, else F.
- It is a linter, not a detector. A clean pass means the text has none of the listed tells, nothing more.
- Fixes only swap characters or delete filler; nothing that changes meaning is auto-fixed.
- `--format` is text, json, github (annotations plus an error line per failing text) or markdown (the table the Action posts as its one review comment).
- A baseline (`--baseline-write`, `--baseline`) keys findings by file, rule and sentence, not line number; only findings outside it fail.
- `--explain <rule>` prints why the pattern reads as machine-made, a line that trips the rule, the same line rewritten, and when to switch the rule off. Every rule carries that material and a test checks its example still trips it.
- `.slop.json` takes `overrides`: `{ files, ignore, only, maxScore }` applied in order to a matching path, later entries winning. `--only` runs named rules alone; `--skip` is another spelling of `--ignore`. Unknown rule ids are rejected.
- `--init` writes `.slop.json`, `--init action` the pull request workflow, `--init hook` the commit-msg hook; it never overwrites an existing file.
- Measured, not asserted: on `bench/corpus`, five public-domain texts written before any language model grade A or B and five pieces of model output grade F. The numbers are rates, not detection accuracy, and the tool never emits a probability.
